les: Moeilike tye, en wat boere daaraan doen
kaps_punt: Geen KABV-inhoudstrepie: KABV Afdeling 2.5 (interafhanklikheid; oorsaak en gevolg; omgee vir die planeet en verantwoordelik optree)

items.bewering: Boerdery hang af van die weer, die grond en die water. Dit loop op 'n plaas skeef as een van hierdie drie nie reg is nie.
items.bron: FAO, Sustainable agriculture and rural development (fao.org/4/U8480E/U8480E0l.htm) names land and water as the natural resource base of farming; Agbiz/IDC survey reporting (Farmers Weekly, BusinessDay 7 Aug 2025) shows weather and drought as the leading production risk. As a set: the lesson does not say 'net' these three, and its own pests-and-diseases block adds further causes, so no false 'only three' is stated.

items.bewering: Boere kan nie die weer beheer nie, maar hulle kan die grond en die water oppas.
items.bron: Consistent with FAO sustainable-agriculture guidance (soil and water conservation as farm-level management) and with the WRC in-field rainwater harvesting work (scielo.org.za/pdf/wsa/v37n5/v37n5a18.pdf). No source treats weather as something a farmer controls.

items.bewering: Die weer is een van die grootste uitdagings vir boere.
items.blok: Te min reën, te veel reën en hael
items.bron: Agbiz/IDC Agribusiness Confidence Index reporting: almost two-thirds of agribusinesses ranked climate volatility as their biggest risk concern in 2024 (BusinessDay / Sunday Times, 7 Aug 2025); El Niño drought named as the main drag on Q1 2024 confidence (Farmers Weekly; africasustainabilitymatters.com). The softened form 'een van die grootste' is supported.

items.bewering: 'n Droogte is 'n lang tyd waarin baie minder reën as gewoonlik op 'n plek val.
items.blok: Te min reën, te veel reën en hael
items.bron: South African Weather Service definition as reported by Africa Check (3 Feb 2016): below-average rainfall over an extended period, normal measured over 30 years; under 75% of normal is severe meteorological drought. https://africacheck.org/2016/02/03/frequently-asked-questions-about-south-africas-drought

items.bewering: Dan groei gewasse swak en het diere minder kos en water.
items.blok: Te min reën, te veel reën en hael
items.bron: Africa Check 2016 (agricultural drought: insufficient moisture for average crop production); Farmers Weekly on locust damage to grazing that had 'regrown after the first good rainfall following a devastating multiple-year drought in the Karoo', i.e. drought had removed the grazing.

items.bewering: Te veel reën kan riviere laat oorloop en die lande onder water sit. So 'n vloed kan lande beskadig en gewasse wegspoel.
items.blok: Te min reën, te veel reën en hael
items.bron: Western Cape Department of Agriculture, 'Damage to Western Cape agriculture infrastructure estimated at R1,053 billion' (westerncape.gov.za/agriculture); BusinessDay 25 Jun and 25 Sep 2023: rivers burst their banks, orchards and vineyards flooded, vegetable and strawberry crops swept away.

items.bewering: Hael is balletjies ys wat tydens donderstorms uit die lug val en vrugte, groente en ander gewasse kan beskadig.
items.blok: Te min reën, te veel reën en hael
items.bron: NOAA NSSL Severe Weather 101: Hail (nssl.noaa.gov/education/svrwx101/hail): solid ice formed inside thunderstorm updrafts, balls or irregular lumps of ice; NHESS 23, 1549 (2023) on Highveld hail and crop damage; Moonstone 2025 on hail losses to farmers.

items.bewering: Plaagdiere is diere, dikwels insekte, wat skade doen, soos aan gewasse of vee.
items.bron: UNEP LEAP glossary 'pests' and Wikipedia 'Pest (organism)': organisms that damage crops, livestock or stored produce; insects the most important group, alongside mites, nematodes, rodents and birds. 'Dikwels' is the right quantifier.

items.bewering: Sprinkane is 'n voorbeeld van plaagdiere wat groot skade kan aanrig.
items.bron: gov.za, Minister Didiza on the brown locust outbreak, 7 Apr 2022 (veld, grazing and crops affected in the Eastern, Northern and Western Cape); Farmers Weekly, 'Vast areas of grazing destroyed by locusts in the Eastern Cape'; SABC News, 'Locust swarms destroy crops in the Karoo'.

items.bewering: Siektes maak plante en diere siek en dan groei hulle nie goed nie.
items.bron: ARC-Small Grain / SA Grain mag 'Knowledge crucial in fight against rust' (2023): leaf and stripe rust can cause more than 50% yield loss on susceptible wheat; Agbiz reporting names animal disease as a standing sector concern.

items.bewering: Roes is 'n plantsiekte wat bruin of oranje kolletjies op die blare van koring of mielies maak.
items.bron: ARC-Small Grain (arc.agric.za, Small Grain Diseases) and SA Grain mag: wheat leaf rust forms orange-brown pustules scattered on the leaves, rusts are fungal; University of Minnesota Extension and UC IPM: common rust of maize forms cinnamon-brown to brick-red pustules on both leaf surfaces. Not stated as 'only' leaves or 'only' these colours, so stem rust (stems) and stripe rust (yellow) do not falsify it.

items.bewering: Gewasse haal uit die grond water en ander stowwe wat hulle nodig het. Party lande word jaar na jaar gebruik sonder dat die grond kans kry om te herstel. Die grond raak dan uitgeput, en ons sê dit word oorbenut.
items.bron: FAO (fao.org/4/x5790e/x5790e0f.htm) and Queensland Government 'Soil fertility decline': soil exhaustion under continuous cropping is the removal of NUTRIENTS in harvested crops faster than they are replaced, plus loss of organic matter and structure. Water taken up by a crop is replaced by the next rain; it is not what runs out year after year. Each sentence is true on its own, but the only substance the chain names is water, so the cause a learner takes away is 'the soil ran out of water'. That is the wrong cause, and it points to the wrong remedy (watering) for a problem the next block solves with rotation and rest. The lesson's own CAPS focus is cause and effect.
items.regstelling: Name what actually runs out: crops take from the soil the food substances (nutrients) that plants need to grow, and when the same field is used year after year without a chance to recover, those substances are used up faster than they come back, so the soil becomes exhausted. Either drop water from this causal sentence or make clear that water is not what gets used up, because rain brings it back.

items.bewering: Op uitgeputte grond is dit moeiliker om gesonde gewasse te verbou. Oor baie jare lewer dieselfde land dan al swakker oeste.
items.bron: FAO (fao.org/4/t0742e/T0742E07.htm): many soils cannot be continuously cultivated without degradation 'marked by decreased crop yields'; Queensland Government 'Soil fertility decline': reserves fall until they cannot meet crop demand, reducing growth and yield. The declining yield is presented as a consequence, not as proof, which is sound.

items.bewering: Uitgeputte grond kan gelukkig weer herstel. Boere kan hul gewasse afwissel deur elke jaar 'n ander gewas op 'n land te plant. Hulle kan 'n land ook 'n ruk lank laat rus.
items.bron: FAO (fao.org/4/t0742e/T0742E07.htm; fao.org/4/y2413e/y2413e0b.htm): fallow periods alternated with cropping maintain soil nutrient fertility, with periodically fallowed plots yielding 40-50% more than continuously cropped ones; CTCN 'Crop rotation' (ctc-n.org): a sequence of different crops on the same ground maintains or increases fertility and prevents the soil exhaustion of a single crop grown repeatedly; legumes in the rotation add nitrogen. 'Elke jaar 'n ander gewas' is one valid form of rotation (cycles of one, two or three years exist); it is not stated as the only form.

items.bewering: Boere kan ook water spaar deur reënwater op te vang en dit net na die lande te lei wat dit nodig het.
items.bron: Water Research Commission-funded in-field rainwater harvesting research (Water SA 37(5), scielo.org.za/pdf/wsa/v37n5/v37n5a18.pdf; UFS and CUT work around Thaba Nchu): runoff from strips is caught and directed into the cropped basins, raising maize and sunflower yields by 30-50%.

items.bewering: Hierdie manier van boer noem ons volhoubare boerdery. Dit beskerm die grond, die water en die natuur vir die toekoms.
items.bron: FAO definition of sustainable agricultural development (fao.org/4/U8480E/U8480E0l.htm): conserves land, water, plant and animal genetic resources, is environmentally non-degrading, and meets needs of present and future generations. As a set, the three practices are given as examples and no single fix is claimed for the weather, pest or disease problems; the opening block already says farmers cannot control the weather.

items.bewering: Voedselverspilling is kos wat geëet kon word, maar wat mense weggooi of laat sleg word.
items.blok: Kos wat in die vullisblik beland
items.bron: FAO definition as cited by TABLE/FCRN 'What is food loss and food waste?' and WUR: 'food appropriate for human consumption being discarded ... or left to spoil'.

items.bewering: Die boer en sy plaaswerkers het die koring geplant en geoes. Fabriekwerkers, vragmotorbestuurders en winkelpersoneel het die brood tot by jou gebring.
items.blok: Kos wat in die vullisblik beland
items.bron: DALRRD Wheat Market Value Chain Profile 2020 and NAMC Food Value Chains: Wheat: farmers and farm workers grow wheat, millers make flour, bakers (including factory bakers) bake, retailers sell; transport links every stage.

items.bewering: Al hulle werk is vermors as die brood in die vullisblik beland. Die water en die brandstof van die hele pad is ook vermors.
items.blok: Kos wat in die vullisblik beland
items.bron: WWF South Africa, 'Five food waste facts that are hard to swallow' and food waste initiative page (wwf.org.za): water and energy embedded in food are lost when it is wasted; diesel and electricity wasted through food waste estimated at about R1 billion a year.

items.bewering: Glossary entry read alone: plaagdier - ''n Dier, dikwels 'n insek, wat skade doen, soos aan gewasse of vee.'
items.bron: UNEP LEAP glossary 'pests'; Wikipedia 'Pest (organism)'. True without its block.

items.bewering: Glossary entry read alone: roes - ''n Plantsiekte wat bruin of oranje kolletjies op die blare maak.'
items.bron: ARC-Small Grain on wheat leaf rust (orange-brown pustules); University of Minnesota Extension on maize common rust (cinnamon-brown pustules). True without its block. It does not separate rust from other leaf-spot diseases and does not say a fungus causes it, but nothing in it is false.

items.bewering: Glossary entry read alone: oorbenut - 'Wanneer grond oor en oor gebruik word sonder kans om te herstel.'
items.bron: Afrikaans usage of 'oorbenutting' for land used beyond its sustainable capacity, leading to soil degradation (SATNT journal article on soil as an exhaustible resource; Unisa GeoTerm). The general word also covers veld, water and other resources; in a soil-only glossary the narrower sense is true.

items.bewering: Glossary entry read alone: volhoubare boerdery - 'Boerdery wat die grond, die water en die natuur vir die toekoms beskerm.'
items.bron: FAO definition of sustainable agricultural development (fao.org/4/U8480E/U8480E0l.htm). True without its block.

items.bewering: Glossary entry read alone: voedselverspilling - 'Kos wat geëet kon word, maar wat mense weggooi of laat sleg word.'
items.bron: FAO definition via TABLE/FCRN and WUR. True without its block.

opsomming: Every claim checks out bar one: the soil-exhaustion block names water as the only thing crops take from the soil before saying the soil becomes exhausted, so it teaches the wrong cause (water, which rain replaces, instead of nutrients) in a lesson whose focus is cause and effect; the superlative 'een van die grootste uitdagings' is supported, and the problems and responses hold up as a set.
